text:
Both teams arrive on Saturday night off wild finishes. Buffalo came back from two goals down to beat Anaheim 7-6, with Tage Thompson scoring three and Roger McQueen getting his first NHL goal. Los Angeles beat Ottawa 6-5 when Quinton Byfield won it in overtime. The Sabres close a four-game road trip, and both clubs are short-handed: Adrian Kempe and Mats Zuccarello are out for the Kings, while Buffalo is missing Justin Danforth, Konsta Helenius and Jiri Kulich.

Neither team has been well served by its results. Our numbers say each is better than its record, with finishing and goaltending costing both. At five on five the Sabres have 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and the Kings 48%, so there's little between them. Our model has Buffalo at 3.07 expected goals tonight and Los Angeles at 2.97. The special-teams matchup to watch is the Kings' power play, which creates 0.82 expected goals a game, against a Buffalo penalty kill that allows the same. In net, projected starters Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (-3.5 goals saved above expected, a measure of saves beyond what the shots should produce) and Anton Forsberg (+0.2) both posted strong figures last season, about +9 each.

With Zuccarello out, Artemi Panarin has moved beside Erik Haula and Alex Laferriere. Panarin has a 37% chance to score and a 74% chance at a point, and Laferriere is goalless in six games despite 3.1 expected goals. For Buffalo, Thompson is the top threat at 36% to score, with Jack Quinn at 30%.
